m57_jean_administrator_outlook.pst
  Version 14 (ANSI, permutative encryption) Outlook 2000 store, 98,304 bytes, one message
  ("Welcome to Microsoft Outlook 2000!"). Extracted unmodified from
  /Documents and Settings/Administrator/Local Settings/Application Data/Microsoft/Outlook/outlook.pst
  of nps-2008-jean.E01 (NPS M57-Jean scenario, Digital Corpora:
  https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/corpora/drives/nps-2008-m57-jean/). A simulated
  workstation image, public for research and teaching. Ground truth for its live content
  was read with libpff (pypff 20260926).

outlook_pst_crate_empty_v23.pst
  Version 23 (Unicode) store with no messages: examples/Empty.pst of the `outlook-pst` 1.1.0
  crate (MIT licence, https://crates.io/crates/outlook-pst). Used to pin the Unicode header,
  page and entry layout only; no Unicode message has been read from real evidence.

nromanoff_v23_libpff_oracle.tsv (store NOT committed)
  Version 23 (Unicode, 64-bit, compressible encryption) store, 59,442,176 bytes, 543 mail and
  contact items, SHA-256 bab64f3589f8ce758df9e595b89a5e4b9be159929e49100397152fdcc7bd6013.
  Public test data of plaso (Apache-2.0), test_data/nromanoff@stark-research-labs.com.pst in
  https://github.com/log2timeline/plaso, held locally at
  ~/forensic_corpora/plaso_pst/nromanoff_stark_research_labs.pst (SOURCE.md there). A
  fictional scenario (Natasha Romanoff, Stark Research Labs). Too large to commit; the tests read it
  from the directory named by SEANCE_PST23_CORPUS and skip without it. The oracle was read with
  pffexport 20231205 (libpff), `pffexport -q -d -l log.txt -m items`: nid is the item identifier it
  logs, attachments the "Saving attachment" lines, subject the Subject line, folder the export path.
  pffexport skips one item, the free/busy message 0x200044 in "Freebusy Data", so it is not listed.
  libpff cannot recover deleted items from this file (`-m recovered` fails at offset 356864), so
  what Seance recovers from it is not libpff-graded.
m57_jean_synthetic_8bit_folder.pst
  SYNTHETIC, never real evidence. m57_jean_administrator_outlook.pst with the second byte of the
  "Sent Items" folder name ("e") replaced by 0xE9, at the three places the name is stored (the
  folder's own property context and its parent's hierarchy table), made by encrypting the byte
  with the permutative table, and the CRC of each touched block recomputed (zero-seeded
  reflected 0xEDB88320, see src/ost4k/crc.rs). SHA-256
  3b47acfc18eb0f8d65770206d604401f60b733f5d3a7235fef6c4b030d0ff3e3. It grades the mechanics of
  the 8-bit folder-name decoding on the live version 14 path (HUNT-281) and says nothing about
  any real mailbox. The store's one message has no recipient table and the linked reader
  refuses it, so this fixture carries no live message text.
